slides.title: Glass can't be found. Wire can.
slides.sub: Tracer wire, warning tape and markers

slides.title: No metal, no signal, no locate.
slides.body: All-dielectric fiber is invisible to a locator. Something metallic has to go in with it.

slides.title: Tracer wire rides along
slides.body: Insulated copper or copper-clad steel, orange for communications, laid in the trench or pulled in with the duct.

slides.title: Continuous and reachable
slides.body: Waterproof connectors at every splice. Bring the wire up at handholes, pedestals and test stations.

slides.title: Warning tape is for diggers
slides.body: Orange ribbon about a foot above the duct. Detectable tape adds a foil core that a locator can trace.

slides.title: Then people must ask
slides.body: US: call 811. Australia: Before You Dig Australia. India has no national one-call yet, so marker posts matter.

slides.title: Make buried fiber findable
items: Access at handholes and test stations
Tape a foot above the duct
Marker balls at bends and splices

Fiber is glass and plastic. A locator can't see it at all.

That is why buried fiber gets a tracer wire, warning tape and marker balls, and why the colour orange means communications. Swipe for how each piece works and what fails first.
